ruling.recommended_action: Send to human review: decide the RD-5 scope of the rider's Guillemard Road consent against the 22:54–23:03 segment (exempt = nil; counts = $3.00 voucher) and the RD-6 account referral on that basis
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI ride: the fare record shows base $3.90, distance $19.15 for 13.58 km, time $7.65, waiting $0.11 and platform $1.47, totalling $32.28, with no surge and no undisclosed item, so the rider's "paid more than the estimate" reduces to metered distance units and only unexplained extra km are refundable [F7][F6][RD-2]. The geometry is settled: 13.6 km actual against an 11.0 km optimal route, with exactly one off-route segment 22:54–23:03 driving 3.77 km where the optimal route covers 1.64 km, adding 2.13 km [F1][F3][RD-1].

The RD-4 incident screen is settled against the driver: no traffic incident was logged near the route during the trip window, so RD-4(a) fails, and the band records cannot exempt the segment on their own — the PIE band-2 window 22:32–22:54 ends exactly when the segment begins, and Braddell Road and the KPE sat at band 3 (20–29 km/h) [F15][F12][F13][F14][F3][RD-4].

That leaves RD-5, which this record does not let me resolve. The rider's consent precedes the segment: the driver asked at 22:51 whether he might "go round via Guillemard Road" and the rider answered at 22:51 "Sure, go ahead.", before the 22:54 segment start, and the chat record is complete and timestamped [F8][F9][F10][F3][RD-5]. But this is a specific named-road authorisation: it covers driving on Guillemard Road only, and the record must tie the segment to that road [F8][F9][RD-5]. No fact carries a road name for the driven path — F3 is distance and stray geometry, and F11 names Guillemard Road only in the driver's post-trip statement, on which he cannot rely to prove the road driven [F3][F11][RD-5]. Nothing places the segment elsewhere either, so the correspondence between the agreed road and the path driven is unreadable, and that undetermined finding moves the amount: if the segment is exempt the refund is nil, if it counts it is 2.13 km at this trip's stated rate [F3][RD-2]. No rider-requested stop excuses it, since the rider named no place and no stop was measured [F8][F9][F3][RD-3].

Because an undetermined element that moves the amount must go to a person, the case is escalated and I issue no award. For the reviewer: if the segment is not exempt, the arithmetic is $19.15 ÷ 13.58 km = $1.4102/km, and 2.13 km × $1.4102/km = $3.0037, i.e. $3.00, issued as a Ryde voucher, with the billed $3.65 excess-distance item containing non-segment mileage that RD-2 leaves unrefunded [F7][F4][F3][RD-2]; the $0.11 metered waiting unit stands and nothing is added under FARE-1 [F5][F7][RD-3][FARE-1]. Whether RD-6's accompanying account referral attaches depends on that same decision — the driver's record shows 2 route disputes in the last 90 days, both upheld — so I leave the account question to the reviewer rather than flagging it myself [F18][F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read every chat message, the driver's statement and the complaint; the exchange is a polite routing question and a short agreement, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11]. The record itself is otherwise complete (measured segment, rate, fare, timestamped chat, traffic records), so the escalation rests on the unreadable scope of consent, not on missing evidence [F3][F4][F7][F10][F12][F15].

rejected_claims.reason: The driver relies on timing as satisfying RD-5, but the rider's 22:51 message [F9] answers the named Guillemard Road proposal [F8], and RD-5 requires a record tying the 22:54–23:03 segment [F3] to that road; timing alone does not, and no fact ties them.

Braddell Road and the KPE at band 3 and fair weather [F13][F14][F16] say nothing about the replaced stretch of the optimal route, which is what RD-4 requires before a diversion is excused.

The rider treats the named-road consent as automatically failing the exemption and the refund as payable, but the tie between the agreed road and the driven path [F3][F8][F9] is undetermined and is for a person to decide, so no award can issue on this record.

The figure of $3.00 is right but the route to it is not: F4 is the billed excess-distance item ($3.65), not the per-km rate; the rate is $19.15 ÷ 13.58 km = $1.4102/km from the fare record [F7], applied to 2.13 km [F3] under RD-2.

The rider asks for a flag_account referral on the driver's 2 upheld route disputes [F18], but RD-6 requires this case to be established against the driver, and no segment finding is established here, so the account action cannot be attached on this record [F17][RD-6].

Correct in outcome but wrong on the clause: the $0.11 is a RydeTAXI metered waiting-time unit [F5], and RD-3 governs rider-requested stops and waiting at them; the unit stands because RD-2 refunds distance units only.
